name: Afghanistan
rule: Agricultural classification of finished sencha remains unresolved. Independently, the enacted 2025 Food/Medicine Anti-Smuggling Law, Articles 22–23, prohibits food import without licence or official permission and expressly covers companies and persons. The no-special-document route is excluded by a conservative inference from that unqualified rule; this is not a blanket tea prohibition.
personalMailApplicability: Articles 22–23 contain no business, resale, minimum-quantity or mode-of-carriage limit; Article 4 includes unlicensed importers and Article 23 names official and unofficial routes. Applying those provisions to a personal purchased postal parcel is an explicit conservative legal-scope inference. Article 21(1)’s separate trade-licence plus Health-permit duty is expressly commercial and is not treated as universal.
authority: Afghanistan Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock; Japan MAFF destination directory
remainingQuestion: No unresolved question prevents the conservative no-special-document exclusion under the independent unqualified 2025 food-permission provisions. A published personal-food exemption or authoritative narrower application of Articles 22–23 could change it. Agricultural classification of finished sencha and current applicability of older agricultural provisions remain unresolved; no agricultural approval/prohibition is inferred from the food law.

30 September independent primary-law check: visually read 2017 Act Article 11 on PDF p.32 (printed p.30). It permits the authority to exempt certain importers for pest-risk analysis/personal use; it does not itself exempt every personal import. The 2019 regulation expressly covers trade or other purposes and consumption, but incorporates the Act’s pest-risk-qualified manufactured-product definition. Retained unresolved because that risk classification remains genuinely undecided.

permitFreeReason: The recovered full operative 2025 law supplies an independent food-permission barrier. Article 22(1) prohibits importing food without licence or official permission;22(2) and 23(1) expressly reach companies and persons, with 23 covering official and unofficial routes. Article 2(13) defines official permission as a Health/Agriculture registered proforma/product-registration certificate, distinct from ordinary Customs declarations. Applying the unqualified 22–23 rule to a 100 g personal parcel is a stated conservative scope inference. Article 21(1) separately limits its dual trading-licence and Health-permit clause to commercial purposes; no express personal-food waiver from 22–23 was found. Agricultural processed-product classification remains unverified.
requiredDocument: Food import licence or official Health/Agriculture permission under 2025 Law Articles 22–23 (personal-post scope inferred from unqualified rule). This is not the ordinary postal customs declaration. Agricultural permit/phytosanitary requirements remain dependent on unresolved manufactured-tea classification.
foodImportReview: Recovered the full 86-page Official Gazette 1472 from the official Justice Ministry database via its published HTTP route and verified a direct identical PDF. Record 18596 is marked in force. Article 2(13) defines permission as a registered proforma/product-registration certificate issued by Health/Agriculture;4 includes unlicensed importers;22 prohibits food import without licence/official permission;23 expressly reaches companies and persons and official/unofficial routes. Articles 22–23 have no commercial-purpose qualifier. Article 21(1) separately uses for commercial purposes, which is preserved as a limitation on that clause and not omitted. The following traveller concession concerns prescription medicines. No automatic personal-food/postal waiver was identified. On an explicit conservative legal-scope inference the separate official-permission rule excludes the no-special-documents route, without resolving agricultural tea classification. The official database marks the 2016 Food Safety Law repealed; that law is not the basis of this decision.
